title: Research: a local traces backend for the operator's machine (Jaeger all-in-one beside Tempo monolithic) is kb facts
goal: kb/public/logs/otel-collector-otlp-pipeline.md gains DOC facts with source rows from the Jaeger docs pinned at a release on Jaeger's all-in-one or v2 binary: its OTLP receiver ports (4317 gRPC, 4318 HTTP) and how to bind them to loopback, its in-memory storage and what a restart loses, its UI port, and its install without a container; beside the Tempo monolithic facts the article has, so the later traces-backend story picks one with the kb's citations

run:
import subprocess, sys
ART = 'kb/public/logs/otel-collector-otlp-pipeline.md'
CASES = [('Which ports does Jaeger all-in-one listen on for OTLP and its UI?', ['all-in-one', '4318'])]
miss = []
for q, terms in CASES:
    out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '_tools/rag.py', 'pack', q, '--root', 'public', '--budget', '2500'],
                         capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    hit = [l for l in out.splitlines() if l.startswith('- ' + ART[len('kb/'):] + ':') and '[DOC' in l
           and all(t.lower() in l.lower() for t in terms)]
    if not hit:
        miss.append((q, terms))
print('missing:', miss if miss else 'none')
sys.exit(1 if miss else 0)
